Hi, that is correct, the Louvain clustering algorithm won't work if there are negative edge weights. Unfortunately this means that `set_brainGraph_attr` will fail. I will definitely add a check in the function for negative weights, and I think I will use one of the solutions in this post: https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/177507/graph-clustering-algorithms-which-consider-negative-weights

As one of the comments states, if the weights have range [-1, 1], then mapping to `abs(x)` might be the best bet. This is also appropriate if *all* weights are negative. Alternatively, I might just switch it to use the "spinglass" method instead of trying to think of every edge case.

Chris

messages.body_plain:
Hi Daniel, I would remove the subject altogether to avoid the headache, but of course if you are studying stroke patients then you wouldn't have a patient group to study! The issue is, as you mention, that some patients will be missing an entire region (or multiple); this fundamentally changes the network structure and where it "falls" among the rest of the patients. The correlations are performed by the function "rcorr" (from the "Hmisc" package), which states in its help file:

"Missing values are deleted in pairs rather than deleting all rows of 'x' having any missing variables."

So yes, I think you should set those to be NA and see if it handles them properly.

Chris

Hi Dan, the format of the file should be a single column in which each row of the file is the volume of each region. The order should match that of "waytotal" and the rows of "fdt_network_matrix" (or whatever connectivity matrix you generate with other software).

I will certainly add some more information to the User Guide. It is sometimes difficult for me to "think like a beginner" in terms of what is unclear in the User Guide and package docs, since I know the package so well. In terms of putting worked examples on Github, I doubt I will be able to add it to the package itself, but other packages have a separate "data" package (for example, there is the "igraphdata" package) that separates the example datasets from the package itself. That is a solution I will look into, but not for this next release. In the meantime, I will be more clear in the User Guide.

Chris
